diagnosis.concreteUnhandledPath: An accepted ordinary touch release with a missing or retargeted compatibility click did not invoke Start or Demolish. Normal periodic HUD updates do not normally replace those Ready controls.

api.clickSuppression: Pure boolean; root capture listener owns preventDefault and stopImmediatePropagation

tests.command: node --test tests/command-pointer-input-v31.test.mjs tests/touch-input.test.mjs tests/draft-pointer-input.test.mjs tests/pinned-recruit-map-v30.test.mjs tests/recipe-marker-input.test.mjs tests/merge-badge-ui.test.mjs

coverage: Touch and pen release invokes actual main Start and Demolish once without native click
Same logical action and full dataset survive replacement of the original node
Caller callbacks revalidate Game, phase, round, selection, actual tower identity, selected enemy and move identity
Disabled, hidden, inert, CSS-hidden and disconnected current release targets reject activation
Retargeted legacy clicks on nonbutton ancestors, canvas or newly exposed controls cannot execute again
Changed wall selection cannot demolish either old or newly selected wall
Native click before pointerup cannot double Start
Drag-return, scroll/blur clear, cancel, capture loss, secondary button and inverse multitouch sequences reject activation and ghost clicks
Forty repeated physical taps remain executable without debounce
Keyboard/AT detail0 and clearly genuine mouse actions remain native
Existing draw, recipe-map, pinned-badge and merge checks pass
Actual Start preserves seeded RNG; actual Demolish preserves gold/CP and clears only the selected foundation
boundaries: Production edits are limited to the new helper; root owns main listeners and identity capture.
The VM invokes actual main handleCommand and Game methods through a small event/DOM fixture. This is not a physical iPad/Safari reproduction.
The helper does not prevent pointerdown defaults, mutate DOM, mutate selection or roll RNG.
Native focus and scrolling remain browser-owned; root connects cancellation.
Root listener wiring and the remaining sixteen-comment UI scope need separate integration/native QA.
